summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including morbid obesity, polymyositis, diastolic heart failure, obstructive sleep apnea, and long-term anticoagulation presented for evaluation of abnormal uterine bleeding. She underwent hysteroscopy, dilation and curettage, cervical biopsy, and Mirena IUD placement as part of her workup and treatment. Due to her multiple comorbidities, she was admitted for overnight observation. She tolerated the procedure well, remained hemodynamically stable, controlled her pain with oral medications, and resumed normal oral intake. Her warfarin was held perioperatively with heparin line flush for thromboprophylaxis and was restarted prior to discharge. She was discharged home the following morning in stable condition with instructions to avoid strenuous activity and follow up with her gynecologist. Biopsy results showed benign endometrial tissue with no evidence of malignancy, though prior Pap findings of atypical glandular cells warranted continued monitoring.
problems: Unspecified disorders of menstruation and other abnormal bleeding from female genital tract
